operations.value:
The projection refresh work added deleteTrackingTaskRefs to reset refs/workbook/remotes/ between local-bare sync samples, on the assumption that stale tracking refs would make a later sample cheaper than a first one. Unreachable defensive code in a measurement harness is a liability: it implies a hazard that may not exist.

Investigated 2026-08-06 at commit c453596. The finding confirms the premise, and the code is in the harness rather than the product.

deleteTrackingTaskRefs is defined at internal/perf/scenarios.go:806-822 and called from one place, the per-sample preparation inside measureLocalBareSyncAgainstNewOrigin at internal/perf/scenarios.go:798. It bulk-deletes refs/workbook/remotes/ via for-each-ref piped into update-ref --stdin before each local-bare sync sample.

It is a no-op today. The product fetch runs git fetch with --no-tags --prune --no-auto-maintenance (internal/gitstore/sync.go:343), so stale tracking refs cannot survive a fetch, and each sample already gets a fresh bare origin. The in-code comment and README:306-308 were already softened to say it is normally a no-op. No test exercises the non-empty branch: the only references in the tree are the definition and that single call site.

Acceptance: either delete the helper and rely on TestMeasureLocalBareSyncPublishesEverySampleToItsOwnOrigin (internal/perf/scenarios_test.go:1391) to keep the per-sample isolation guarantee, or add a test that seeds stale tracking refs so the non-empty branch is actually exercised. Removal is the smaller diff and matches this tasks stated preference. Whichever is chosen, update README:306-308 to match, so the documented rationale and the code agree.

---

**Correction (2026-08-10, PR #71):** the central claim above was refuted during implementation. deleteTrackingTaskRefs is NOT a no-op: each sample's second measured sync (sync-unchanged-local-bare) populates the tracking namespace, so from the second sample onward the reset removes real refs. Leaving them uncleared inflates sync-initial-local-bare by ~25% on the default 500-task fixture — roughly half from the stale namespace being present in the ref store during the measured command, half from the product pruning it inside the measurement. The helper was kept and pinned by a non-vacuous test rather than deleted. The original 2026-08-06 investigation reasoned about a single sample instead of the two-sync-per-sample loop.
